Supporting Learning and Teaching@Lingnan is a professional development programme for Lingnan University staff and is mandatory for postgraduate students with teaching duties. You should join SLT@Lingnan if you are:

- An early-career faculty member with fewer than three years of teaching experience*

- A postgraduate student with teaching duties*

- A staff member who directly supports learning, such as librarians or OSA ILP officers

items.event_title: [SOCSP Sociology Seminar Series 2026 - 2027] Caring for Self and Others: Compassion and Well-being in Later Life
items.event_detail:
In this session, Prof. Leung Kui-yi Dara from the Department of Social Work, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, will deliver a seminar titled  "Caring for Self and Others: Compassion and Well-being in Later Life".

Abstract:
Compassion is often viewed as a personal quality, yet it is also shaped by the relationships and environments in which people live. This seminar brings together findings from a series of studies examining how compassion operates in later life among family caregivers and older couples. Drawing on both quantitative and qualitative research, the presentation explores how self-compassion may support individuals in caring for others, how compassionate experiences are influenced by close relationships and social contexts, and how compassion relates to psychological and relational well-being. Findings suggest that compassion is not only an individual resource but also a relational process that is shaped by interactions with significant others and broader social environments. By examining compassion across different later-life contexts, this seminar highlights the importance of personal, relational, and contextual factors in supporting well-being, meaningful relationships, and healthy ageing.

items.event_title: Division of Science Seminar Series: Mechanisms of change on New Zealand rocky shores
items.event_detail:
The Division of Science (DoS) Seminar Series is back! All are welcome!

In 2026/27 Term 1, the DoS has invited 4 academic speakers to share science learning with public. 

*1 Unit of ILP Credit will be awarded to full attendance. (This is applicable to LU undergraduates)*

About the first seminar: 
The intertidal zone of rocky shores is one of the most abiotically variable and physiologically stressful environments on earth. Organisms are exposed to marine conditions at low tide and terrestrial conditions at high tide, meaning they are vulnerable to both marine and atmospheric extremes, especially heatwaves or one-off events. In this seminar, I will discuss my research on limpet ecophysiology. Mainly, how these common grazing gastropods respond to heat stress, what are their physiological tolerances, how variable are they, and how they manifest at large- and small-scales. I will also talk about some of my work on long-term changes and poleward range shifts.  

Speaker: 
Dr. Spencer Virgin is a postdoctoral fellow in the School of Biological sciences here at  University of Canterbury. He completed his PhD at UC in 2023 with David Schiel and Mark Denny (Stanford) as his supervisors. Prior to that, he worked as a conservation programs specialist designing and implementing salt marsh restoration projects in Maritime Canada after completing his MSc on the thermal tolerances of larval mussels and impacts of fine-scale heterogeneity on adults.

KINO Series#16: Film Screening & Post-Screening Talk of PALIMPSEST: THE STORY OF A NAME《隱蹟之書：重寫自我》
items.event_detail:
ILP: 2.5 units (Aesthetic Development)
講者 Speaker: 雪美蓮導演 Dir. Mary Stephen 
主持 Moderators: 葉月瑜教授 Prof. Emilie Yeh, 胡靜女士 Ms. Hu Jing

資深剪接師雪美蓮，總想不透自己的姓氏到底姓史蒂芬，還是姓雪、姓陳？明明生於典型華人家庭，何解會取洋人姓？翻開父親留下的筆記，赫然發現祖先竟是澳洲土著，母親年輕時懷抱文學理想，更疑似協助吳爾芙外甥與凌叔華密會。身世之謎愈看愈撲朔迷離，她化身偵探親自追查，穿梭於時代風雲與家庭影像，以「史蒂芬」為圓心拼貼家族秘史。殖民、戰亂、身分流動⋯⋯真相與虛構層層交疊，孰能分辨？榮獲金馬獎最佳紀錄片與最佳剪輯，在不斷謄寫、抹去與覆寫的家族史與記憶中探尋實相，重寫自我故事。
Spanning eight decades and four continents, filmmaker and editor Mary Stephen embarks on a personal investigation into her English surname. It is not intended to be a narcissistic exploration but rather an effort to uncover the dissonances and the contradictions in our heritage that, in spite of our all-too-human desire for harmony and continuity, are the fundamental elements that shape us. It is in this spirit that this intimate journey unfolds.
